newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Schiphol consortium takes control of JFK terminal.
newsitem.headline: Schiphol consortium takes control of JFK terminal.

text.p: A consortium including Amsterdam's Schiphol airport on Tuesday took over management of the International Arrivals Building (terminal four) at New York's John F.Kennedy International Airport, Schiphol said.
The JFKIAT consortium will initiate a phased replacement of the facility with a new terminal in a project costing around two billion guilders and financed by a recent bond issue.

The contract with the Port Authority of New York and New Jersey provides for an initial management period to 2015, Schiphol said. The new terminal is expected to be finished in 2001 and will have a capacity of six million passengers a year.

Schiphol USA Inc, a unit of Schiphol's international division Schiphol Management Services, has a 40 percent participation in JFKIAT. Investment bank Lehman Brothers has 20 percent and project developer LCOR JFK the remaining 40 percent. ((-- Amsterdam newsroom +31 20 504 5000, Fax +31 20 504 5040))
